translations.literal: On a mission to Jin, when he reached Yanshan, the Wanyan who hosted the banquet had a name that violated taboo names of Emperor Renzong's temple; Jia firmly declined, and Wanyan changed his name to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: While on a mission to Jin, he reached Yanshan, where the Wanyan who hosted the banquet bore a name that violated taboo names associated with Emperor Renzong; Jia firmly refused to attend, and the man changed his name to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 自紹興後，凡出疆遇忌，俱辭設宴，皆不得免，秦檜所定也。

translations.literal: Since the Shaoxing era, whenever envoys crossed the border on days of mourning taboo, they all declined banquets yet could never avoid them—a rule established by Qin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Shaoxing era, whenever envoys went abroad on days of mourning taboo, they all declined banquets but could never escape them—a practice Qin Hui had established.

sentences.zh: 九月三日，金宴甲，以宣仁聖烈后忌，辭。

translations.literal: On the third day of the ninth month, the Jin held a banquet for Jia; citing the mourning day for Empress Xuanren the Sacred and Majestic, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the ninth month the Jin held a banquet for Jia; citing the mourning observance for Empress Xuanren the Sacred and Majestic, he declined to attend.

sentences.zh: 還除司農少卿，進太常，擢權工部侍郎，升同修撰，除寶謨閣待制，知江陵府，湖北安撫使。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Vice Minister of Agriculture, promoted to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, elevated to Acting Vice Minister of Works, advanced to Co-authoring Compiler, appointed Awaiting Secretariat Drafter at the Baomo Pavilion, made Prefect of Jiangling, and Military Commissioner for Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was appointed Vice Minister of Agriculture, then promoted through the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to Acting Vice Minister of Works and Co-authoring Compiler; he was made Awaiting Secretariat Drafter at the Baomo Pavilion, Prefect of Jiangling, and Military Commissioner for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 甲謂：「荊州為吳、蜀脊，高保融分江流，瀦之以為北海，太祖常令決去之，蓋保江陵之要害也。」

translations.literal: Jia said: "Jingzhou is the backbone between Wu and Shu. Gao Baorong divided the river's flow and dammed it to form the Northern Sea. Emperor Taizu often ordered it breached and removed—this was to secure Jiangling's strategic position."
translations.idiomatic: Jia said, "Jingzhou is the backbone between Wu and Shu. Gao Baorong diverted the river and dammed it to create the Northern Sea. Emperor Taizu repeatedly ordered those works torn down, for they were meant to hold Jiangling's vital ground."

sentences.zh: 即因遺址浚築，亙四十里。

translations.literal: He immediately dug and built on the old site, extending forty li.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dredged and built on the old site, extending the works forty li.

sentences.zh: 移知廬州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 程松為四川宣撫使，吳曦副之，以甲知興元府、利東安撫使。

translations.literal: Cheng Song was Sichuan Military Commissioner and Wu Xi his deputy; Jia was made Prefect of Xingyuan and Military Commissioner for Eastern Li.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Song served as Sichuan Military Commissioner with Wu Xi as his deputy; Jia was appointed Prefect of Xingyuan and Military Commissioner for Eastern Li.

sentences.zh: 時蜀口出師敗衄，金陷西和、成州，曦焚河池縣。

translations.literal: At that time armies sent from the Shu frontier were defeated; the Jin captured Xihe and Chengzhou, and Xi burned Hechi County.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies sent from the Shu frontier were routed; the Jin took Xihe and Chengzhou, and Xi burned Hechi County.

sentences.zh: 先是，曦已遣姚淮源獻四州於金，金鑄印立曦為蜀王。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi had already sent Yao Huaiyuan to cede four prefectures to the Jin; the Jin cast a seal and installed Xi as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xi had already sent Yao Huaiyuan to surrender four prefectures to the Jin; the Jin cast a seal and enthroned Xi as King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 甲時在漢嘉，未至鎮也。

translations.literal: Jia was then at Hanjia and had not yet reached his post.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was then at Hanjia and had not yet arrived to take up his command.

sentences.zh: 金人破大散關，興元都統制毋思以重兵守關，而曦陰徹驀關之戍，金自板岔谷繞出關後，思挺身免。

translations.literal: The Jin broke through Dasanguan. The overall commander of Xingyuan, Wu Si, held the pass with heavy troops, but Xi secretly withdrew the garrison at Moguang Pass; the Jin circled around via Bancha Valley from behind the pass, and Si escaped alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin broke through Dasanguan. Wu Si, overall commander at Xingyuan, held the pass with a large force, but Xi secretly pulled back the garrison at Moguang Pass; the Jin slipped around through Bancha Valley from behind the pass, and Si escaped by himself.

sentences.zh: 甲告急於朝，乞下兩宣撫司協力捍禦。

translations.literal: Jia urgently reported to court, requesting orders to both Military Commission offices to join forces in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jia sent an urgent report to court, asking that both military commission offices be ordered to combine their efforts in defense.

sentences.zh: 松謀遁，甲固留不可，遽以便宜檄甲兼沿邊制置。

translations.literal: Song planned to flee; Jia firmly detained him and would not allow it, then immediately issued an expedient order appointing Jia concurrently as Frontier Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Song planned to flee, but Jia firmly kept him from leaving; he then immediately issued an expedient order appointing Jia concurrently as Frontier Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 曦遣後軍統制王鉞、準備將趙觀以書致甲，甲援大義拒之，因臥疾。

translations.literal: Xi sent Rear Army Commander Wang Yue and Ready General Zhao Guan with letters to Jia; Jia cited righteous principle to refuse, then took to bed claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent Rear Army Commander Wang Yue and Ready General Zhao Guan with letters to Jia; Jia invoked higher duty to refuse them and then took to his bed, feigning illness.

sentences.zh: 曦又遣其弟文邀甲相見，甲叱而去之。

translations.literal: Xi again sent his younger brother Wen to invite Jia to meet; Jia scolded him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Xi again sent his younger brother Wen to invite Jia to a meeting; Jia rebuked him and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 乃援顏真卿河北故事，欲自拔歸朝，先募二兵持帛書遣參知政事李壁告變，且曰：「若遣吳總以右職入川，即日可瓦解矣。」

translations.literal: He then invoked the precedent of Yan Zhenqing in Hebei, intending to extricate himself and return to court; first he recruited two soldiers to carry a silk letter to Vice Grand Councilor Li Bi reporting the rebellion, saying: "If Wu Zong is sent into Sichuan with a high appointment, the rebellion can be dissolved that very day."
translations.idiomatic: He then invoked the precedent of Yan Zhenqing in Hebei, intending to break free and return to court; first he recruited two soldiers to carry a silk letter to Vice Grand Councilor Li Bi reporting the treason, saying, "If Wu Zong is sent into Sichuan with a high appointment, the rebellion can collapse that very day."

sentences.zh: 曦僭王位，甲遂去官。

translations.literal: When Xi presumptuously assumed royal rank, Jia then resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi presumptuously declared himself king, Jia resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 朝廷久乃微聞曦反狀，韓侂胄猶不之信，甲奏至，舉朝震駭。

translations.literal: The court had long vaguely heard of Xi's rebellion but Han Tuozhou still did not believe it; when Jia's memorial arrived, the whole court was shocked.
translations.idiomatic: The court had long had vague reports of Xi's rebellion, yet Han Tuozhou still refused to believe them; when Jia's memorial arrived, the entire court was shaken.

sentences.zh: 壁袖帛書進，上覽之，稱「忠臣」者再。

translations.literal: Bi presented the silk letter from his sleeve; the emperor read it and twice called him a "loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Bi produced the silk letter from his sleeve; after reading it, the emperor twice called Jia a "loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 召甲赴行在，命吳總以雜學士知鄂州，多賜告身、金錢，使招諭諸軍為入蜀計。

translations.literal: Jia was summoned to the temporary capital; Wu Zong was appointed Miscellaneous Academician and Prefect of Ezhou, and many official commissions and cash were granted to summon and persuade the armies for the plan to enter Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was summoned to the temporary capital; Wu Zong was appointed Miscellaneous Academician and prefect of Ezhou, and large grants of commissions and cash were given to rally the armies for the plan to enter Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 復命以帛書賜甲曰：「所乞致仕，實難允從，已降指揮，召赴行在。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to confer a silk letter upon Jia, saying: "Your request to retire is truly hard to grant; orders have already been issued summoning you to the temporary capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court again ordered a silk letter sent to Jia, saying, "Your request to retire truly cannot be granted; orders have already been issued summoning you to the temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷已遣使與金通和，襄、漢近日大捷，北兵悉已渡江而去。

translations.literal: The court has now sent envoys to negotiate peace with the Jin; Xiang and Han have recently won great victories, and northern troops have all crossed the river and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The court has now sent envoys to negotiate peace with the Jin; Xiang and Han have recently won great victories, and the northern armies have all crossed the Yangzi and withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 恐蜀遠未知，更在審度事宜，從長區處。」

translations.literal: Fearing that distant Sichuan may not yet know this, you should further weigh affairs and handle them according to the larger plan."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that distant Sichuan may not yet know this, you should weigh the situation carefully and act according to the larger plan."

sentences.zh: 二兵皆補官。

translations.literal: Both soldiers were granted official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Both messengers were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 甲舟行至重慶，聞安丙等誅曦，復還漢中，上奏待罪。

translations.literal: Jia traveled by boat to Chongqing, heard that An Bing and others had executed Xi, returned to Hanzhong, and submitted a memorial accepting blame.
translations.idiomatic: Jia traveled by boat as far as Chongqing; when he learned that An Bing and others had executed Xi, he returned to Hanzhong and submitted a memorial accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 詔趣還任。

translations.literal: An edict urged him to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to hurry back to his post.

sentences.zh: 甲奏叛臣子孫族屬及附偽罪狀，公論快之。

translations.literal: Jia memorialized on the crimes of rebel officials' descendants, clans, and those who attached themselves to the usurper; public opinion rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Jia memorialized on the punishment of rebel officials' descendants, clans, and those who had joined the usurper, to the great satisfaction of public opinion.

sentences.zh: 會宣撫副使安丙以楊巨源自負倡義之功，陰欲除之，語在《巨源傳》。

translations.literal: At this time Deputy Military Commissioner An Bing, taking pride in Yang Juyuan's merit in initiating righteous action, secretly wished to eliminate him—the account is in the 《Biography of Juyuan》.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Deputy Military Commissioner An Bing, proud of Yang Juyuan's role in launching the righteous uprising, secretly sought to eliminate him—the full account appears in the 《Biography of Juyuan》.

sentences.zh: 巨源既死，軍情叵測，除甲宣撫使。

translations.literal: After Juyuan died, army morale was unpredictable; Jia was appointed Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Juyuan died, army morale became uncertain, and Jia was appointed Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 楊輔亦以為請，當國者疑輔避事，李壁曰：「昔吳璘屬疾，孝宗嘗密詔汪應辰權宣撫司事，既而璘果死，應辰即日領印，軍情遂安，此的例也。」

translations.literal: Yang Fu also requested this; those in power suspected Fu was shirking, but Li Bi said: "Formerly when Wu Lin was gravely ill, Emperor Xiaozong secretly ordered Wang Yingchen to administer the Military Commission Office; soon Lin indeed died, and Yingchen took the seal that very day, and army morale was settled—this is the exact precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu also made the same request; those in power suspected Fu was avoiding responsibility, but Li Bi said, "When Wu Lin fell gravely ill, Emperor Xiaozong secretly ordered Wang Yingchen to administer the Military Commission Office; Lin soon died, and Yingchen took the seal that very day, settling army morale—this is the exact precedent."

sentences.zh: 乃以密劄命甲，甲鐍藏之。

translations.literal: Jia was then secretly ordered by sealed memo; Jia locked it away in storage.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was then secretly ordered by sealed memo, and he locked the document away.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金自鶻嶺關劄金崖，進屯八里山，甲分兵進守諸關，截潼川戍兵駐饒風以待之。

translations.literal: Before long, the Jin moved from Heguling Pass to Zajin Cliff and advanced to encamp at Bali Mountain; Jia divided troops to advance and guard the passes, intercepted Tongchuan garrison troops and stationed them at Raofeng to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jin moved from Heguling Pass to Zajin Cliff and advanced to encamp at Bali Mountain; Jia divided his forces to hold the passes, diverted Tongchuan garrison troops, and stationed them at Raofeng to await the enemy.

sentences.zh: 金人知有備，引去。

translations.literal: The Jin, knowing there were preparations, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that defenses were ready, the Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，上念甲精忠，拜寶謨閣學士，賜衣帶、鞍馬。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, the emperor, mindful of Jia's loyal devotion, appointed him Academician at the Baomo Pavilion and bestowed robes, belt, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed, the emperor, remembering Jia's loyal devotion, appointed him Academician at the Baomo Pavilion and bestowed robes, a belt, a saddle, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 是歲，和議成，朝廷聞彭輅與丙不協，以書問甲，又俾諭丙減汰諸軍勿過甚，及訪蜀人才之可用者。

translations.literal: That year peace was concluded; the court heard that Peng Luo and Bing were at odds, questioned Jia by letter, also instructing him to tell Bing not to reduce and cull troops excessively, and to inquire about usable talent in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: That year a peace settlement was reached; hearing that Peng Luo and Bing were at odds, the court questioned Jia by letter, also instructing him to urge Bing not to cut the armies too deeply and to report on usable talent in Shu.

sentences.zh: 蓋自楊輔召歸，西邊諸事，朝論多於甲取決，人無知者。

translations.literal: From the time Yang Fu was recalled, on western frontier affairs the court's deliberations largely took Jia's judgment as decisive—though no one knew it.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Yang Fu was recalled, the court largely settled western frontier affairs according to Jia's judgment—though almost no one knew it.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，蜀軍無見糧，創為科糴。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era, Shu armies had no cash grain rations, and the practice of assessed grain purchase was created.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing era, Shu armies had no cash rations for grain, and the system of assessed grain purchase was introduced.

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞其病民，命總領李蘩以本所錢招糴，懼不給，又命勸糴其半，「勸糴」之名自此始。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong heard it harmed the people and ordered Overall Supervisor Li Fan to use the office's funds for open purchase; fearing insufficient supply, he further ordered encouraged purchase of half—the name "encouraged purchase" began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong heard that it burdened the people and ordered Overall Supervisor Li Fan to use office funds for open-market purchase; fearing shortfalls, he further ordered that half be obtained by encouraged purchase—the term "encouraged purchase" dates from this.

sentences.zh: 久之，李昌圖總計，復奏令金、梁守倅任責收糴，而勸糴遂罷。

translations.literal: After a long time, Li Changtu as Overall Fiscal Officer again memorialized to assign Jin and Liang prefects and vice-prefects responsibility for collecting purchase grain, and encouraged purchase was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Li Changtu, as Overall Fiscal Officer, again memorialized that the prefects and vice-prefects of Jin and Liang should be held responsible for collecting purchase grain, and encouraged purchase was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 及是，宣、總司令金洋、興元三郡勸糴小麥三十萬石，甲乞下總所照李蘩成法措置，從之。

translations.literal: At this time the Military Commission and Overall Supervisor ordered the three prefectures of Jin, Yang, and Xingyuan to encouraged purchase of three hundred thousand shi of wheat; Jia requested the Overall Office apply Fan's established methods, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Military Commission and Overall Supervisor ordered the three prefectures of Jin, Yang, and Xingyuan to encouraged purchase of three hundred thousand shi of wheat; Jia asked that the Overall Office follow Fan's established methods, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷宣撫司，合利東、西為一帥，治興元，移甲知潼川府。

translations.literal: The next year the Military Commission Office was abolished; Eastern and Western Li were merged under one commander based at Xingyuan; Jia was transferred to Prefect of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Military Commission Office was abolished; Eastern and Western Li were merged under a single commander based at Xingyuan, and Jia was transferred to prefect of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 安丙既同知樞密院事，董居誼為制置使，甲進寶謨閣學士、知興元府、利路安撫使，節制本路屯駐軍馬。

translations.literal: An Bing having become Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Dong Juyi was made Frontier Commissioner; Jia was promoted to Baomo Academician, Prefect of Xingyuan, Military Commissioner of Li Circuit, controlling stationed troops of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Once An Bing had become Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Dong Juyi was made Frontier Commissioner; Jia was promoted to Baomo Academician, Prefect of Xingyuan, and Military Commissioner of Li Circuit, with authority over the circuit's stationed troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷計居誼猶在道，命甲權四川制置司事。

translations.literal: The court reckoning Juyi was still en route, ordered Jia to administer Sichuan Frontier Commission affairs on an interim basis.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting that Juyi was still on the road, the court ordered Jia to administer Sichuan Frontier Commission affairs on an interim basis.

sentences.zh: 先是，大臣撫蜀者，諸將事之，有所謂「互送禮」，實賄賂也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when great ministers pacified Shu, generals attended upon them with what was called "mutual gift-giving"—in fact bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when great ministers governed Shu, the generals waited on them with what was called "mutual gift-giving"—in reality bribery.

sentences.zh: 甲下令首罷之，凡丙所立茶鹽柴邸悉廢之。

translations.literal: Jia ordered its abolition first; all tea, salt, and fuel depots established by Bing were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jia ordered this practice abolished first, and all the tea, salt, and fuel depots Bing had established were dismantled.

sentences.zh: 又乞以皂郊博易鋪場還隸沔戎司，復通吳氏莊，歲收租四萬斛有奇，錢十三萬，以裨總計。

translations.literal: He also requested returning the Zaojiao exchange market to the jurisdiction of the Mian Frontier Command, restored passage to the Wu family estate, yielding over forty thousand shi of rent grain annually and one hundred thirty thousand in cash, to supplement the overall fiscal accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Zaojiao exchange market be returned to the Mian Frontier Command, restored access to the Wu family estate, and reported annual rents of more than forty thousand shi of grain and one hundred thirty thousand strings of cash to supplement the overall fiscal accounts.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 丙增多田稅，甲命屬吏討論，由一府言之，歲減凡百六十萬緡、米麥萬七千石，邊民感泣。

translations.literal: Bing had increased field taxes; Jia ordered subordinate officials to review and discuss; speaking for one prefecture alone, annual reductions totaled 1.6 million strings of cash and seventeen thousand shi of rice and wheat; frontier people wept with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had raised field taxes; Jia ordered his subordinates to review the levies, and for one prefecture alone annual reductions came to 1.6 million strings of cash and seventeen thousand shi of rice and wheat; frontier people wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年，卒於官，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he died in office, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiading reign he died in office at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 甲幼孤多難，母病，刲股以進。

translations.literal: Jia was orphaned young and faced many hardships; when his mother was ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to offer it as medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and beset by hardship, Jia once cut flesh from his thigh to offer his ailing mother as medicine.

sentences.zh: 生平常謂：「吾無他長，惟足履實地。」

translations.literal: Throughout his life he often said: "I have no other talent—only that my feet tread solid ground."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he often said, "I have no other gift—only that my feet walk on solid ground."

sentences.zh: 晝所為，夜必書之，名曰「自監」。

translations.literal: Whatever he did by day, he invariably wrote at night—he called it "Self-Supervision."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he did by day he recorded at night in a journal he called "Self-Supervision."

sentences.zh: 為文平淡，有奏議十卷。

translations.literal: His writing was plain and restrained; he left ten scrolls of memorials and proposals.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was plain and restrained; he left ten scrolls of memorials and policy proposals.

sentences.zh: 理宗詔謚「清惠」。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong posthumously granted the title "Pure and Gracious."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong posthumously granted him the title "Pure and Gracious."

sentences.zh: 楊輔，字嗣勲，遂寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, styled Sikun, was a man of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, whose style name was Sikun, came from Suining.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年進士甲科，召試館職，除秘書省正字，遷校書郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao he passed jinshi in first rank, was summoned to examination for an institute post, appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat, and promoted to Collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qiandao reign he passed the jinshi examination in the top rank, was summoned for an institute examination, appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat, and promoted to Collator.

sentences.zh: 出知眉州，累遷戶部郎中、總領四川財賦，升太府少卿、利西安撫使。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Meizhou, rose through offices to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, Overall Supervisor of Sichuan finances, elevated to Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse and Military Commissioner of Western Li.
translations.idiomatic: He served outside the capital as prefect of Meizhou, rose through successive posts to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Overall Supervisor of Sichuan finances, and was elevated to Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse and Military Commissioner of Western Li.

sentences.zh: 吳挺病，輔以吳氏世帥武興，久恐生變，密白二府，早擇人望以鎮方面。

translations.literal: Wu Ting fell ill; Fu, considering the Wu family's hereditary command of Wuxing, feared that prolonged illness might breed trouble, secretly reported to the two bureaus to early select a man of standing to secure the region.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Ting fell ill, Fu, knowing the Wu family had long commanded Wuxing hereditarily, feared trouble if the illness dragged on and secretly reported to the two bureaus that they should early choose a man of standing to stabilize the region.

sentences.zh: 又貽書四川制置丘崈言：「統制官李奭乃吳氏腹心，緩急不可令權軍。」

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Sichuan Frontier Commissioner Qiu Jun, saying: "Commander Li Shang is the Wu family's inner confidant—in crisis he must not be allowed to take interim command of the army."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Sichuan Frontier Commissioner Qiu Jun, saying, "Commander Li Shang is the Wu family's trusted insider—in an emergency he must not be allowed to take interim command of the army."

sentences.zh: 崈然之。

translations.literal: Jun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 挺卒，崈檄輔權帥事，輔謂：「職為王人，若輕往，第疑軍心。」

translations.literal: When Ting died, Jun ordered Fu by dispatch to administer command affairs; Fu said: "My office is that of the emperor's representative—if I go lightly, it will only raise doubts in army hearts."
translations.idiomatic: When Ting died, Jun dispatched Fu to take interim command; Fu said, "My office is that of the emperor's representative—if I go casually, I will only sow doubt in the army."

sentences.zh: 遂索印即益昌領事。

translations.literal: He then demanded the seal and took charge at Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: He then demanded the seal and assumed command at Yichang.

sentences.zh: 復數月，奏以權興州事楊虞仲兼權。

translations.literal: After several more months, he memorialized that Yang Yuzhong, interim administrator of Xingzhou, be given concurrent interim command.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he memorialized that Yang Yuzhong, who was administering Xingzhou on an interim basis, be given concurrent interim command.

sentences.zh: 召守秘書監、禮部侍郎，以顯謨閣待制知江陵府，移襄陽，又移潼川。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Director of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, appointed as Awaiting Secretariat Drafter at the Xianmo Pavilion and Prefect of Jiangling, transferred to Xiangyang, then again to Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Director of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, appointed Awaiting Secretariat Drafter at the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Jiangling, then transferred to Xiangyang and later to Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 召還，除顯謨閣直學士，奉外祠，尋以敷文閣直學士知成都府、兼本路安撫使。

translations.literal: Recalled, appointed as Direct Academician at the Xianmo Pavilion, granted an outside temple posting; soon made Direct Academician at the Fuwen Pavilion, Prefect of Chengdu, concurrently Military Commissioner of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was appointed Direct Academician at the Xianmo Pavilion and granted an outside temple posting; soon afterward he became Direct Academician at the Fuwen Pavilion, prefect of Chengdu, and concurrently Military Commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄決意用兵，以吳曦為四川宣撫副使，假以節制財利之權。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou was determined to use force; Wu Xi was made Deputy Sichuan Military Commissioner, lent authority over finances and revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was determined to go to war; Wu Xi was made Deputy Sichuan Military Commissioner and given authority over finances and revenue.

sentences.zh: 輔知曦有異志，貽書大臣言：「自昔兵帥與計臣不相統攝，故總領有報發覺察之權。

translations.literal: Fu knew Xi had divergent intentions and sent letters to chief ministers, saying: "Formerly military commanders and fiscal officers were not under unified authority, so the overall supervisor had power to report, investigate, and oversee.
translations.idiomatic: Fu saw that Xi harbored rebellious intentions and wrote to the chief ministers, saying, "In the past military commanders and fiscal officers were not under unified command, so the overall supervisor had the power to report, investigate, and oversee.

sentences.zh: 今所在皆受節制，內憂不輕。」

translations.literal: Now all everywhere are subject to his control—a domestic worry of no light weight."
translations.idiomatic: Now everyone everywhere is subject to his control—a domestic threat of no small weight."

sentences.zh: 因託言他事，遣人以礬書告於朝。

translations.literal: Using another matter as pretext, he sent someone with an invisible-ink letter to report to court.
translations.idiomatic: Under the cover of another matter, he sent a messenger with an invisible-ink letter to report to court.

sentences.zh: 朔日，率官屬東望拜表如常儀。

translations.literal: On the first of the month, he led his staff to face east and submit a memorial in the usual ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the month he led his staff to face east and submit a memorial in the usual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 上意輔能誅曦，密詔授寶謨閣學士、四川制置使，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Fu could execute Xi and secretly ordered him appointed Baomo Academician and Sichuan Frontier Commissioner, permitted to act on his own authority as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Fu could eliminate Xi and secretly ordered him appointed Baomo Academician and Sichuan Frontier Commissioner, with permission to act on his own authority as expedient.

sentences.zh: 時人望輔倡義，劉光祖、李道傳皆勉之。

translations.literal: At the time people looked to Fu to initiate righteous action; Liu Guangzu and Li Daozhuan both urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: At the time public opinion looked to Fu to lead the righteous uprising; Liu Guangzu and Li Daozhuan both urged him forward.

sentences.zh: 輔自以不習兵事，且內郡無兵可用，遷延兩月，但為去計。

translations.literal: Fu himself felt he was unskilled in military affairs, and moreover the inner prefecture had no troops usable; he delayed two months, only planning departure.
translations.idiomatic: Fu himself felt unversed in military affairs, and moreover his inner prefecture had no usable troops; he delayed two months and did nothing but plan his departure.

sentences.zh: 曦移輔知遂寧府，輔遂以印授通判韓植而去。

translations.literal: Xi transferred Fu to Prefect of Suining; Fu then handed the seal to Vice Prefect Han Zhi and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xi transferred Fu to prefect of Suining; Fu then handed the seal to Vice Prefect Han Zhi and departed.

sentences.zh: 安丙、楊巨源密謀誅曦，以輔有人望，謂密詔自輔所來，聞者皆信。

translations.literal: An Bing and Yang Juyuan secretly plotted to execute Xi; since Fu enjoyed public esteem, they said the secret edict came from Fu—and all who heard believed it.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing and Yang Juyuan secretly plotted to kill Xi; because Fu enjoyed public esteem, they claimed the secret edict had come from him, and all who heard it believed them.

sentences.zh: 曦既誅，丙趣輔還成都，除四川宣撫使。

translations.literal: After Xi was executed, Bing urged Fu to return to Chengdu and appointed him Sichuan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xi had been executed, Bing pressed Fu to return to Chengdu and made him Sichuan Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「臣以衰病軟懦，而居建元功者之上，徒恐牽制敗事。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your servant, worn by age and illness and soft and timid, yet placed above those who established the primary achievement—I fear only that I will hamper and ruin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Your servant is aged, ill, and timid, yet placed above those who won the decisive victory—I fear I will only hinder and ruin affairs.

sentences.zh: 安丙才力強濟，賞罰明果，乞以事任付丙。」

translations.literal: An Bing's talent and strength are vigorous and effective, his rewards and punishments clear and decisive—I beg that affairs and responsibility be entrusted to Bing."
translations.idiomatic: An Bing is forceful and capable, with clear and decisive rewards and punishments—I beg that responsibility be entrusted to him."

sentences.zh: 又論：「蜀中三帥，惟武興事權特重，故致今日之變。

translations.literal: He further argued: "Among the three commanders in Shu, only Wuxing's authority was exceptionally heavy—thus leading to today's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued, "Among the three commanders in Shu, only Wuxing's authority was unusually great—thus leading to today's disaster.

sentences.zh: 乞並置兩帥，分其營屯、隸屬。」

translations.literal: I request establishing two commanders jointly, dividing their camps, stations, and subordination."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that two commanders be established side by side, dividing their camps, garrisons, and chains of command."

sentences.zh: 安丙奏乞兩宣撫分司，朝廷察丙與輔異，召輔赴闕。

translations.literal: An Bing memorialized requesting two Military Commissions as separate offices; the court perceived Bing and Fu were at odds and summoned Fu to court.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing memorialized asking that two military commissions be established as separate offices; the court saw that Bing and Fu were at odds and summoned Fu to court.

sentences.zh: 議者謂蜀亂初平，如輔未宜去，乃復以為制置使兼知成都府。

translations.literal: Deliberators said that with Shu unrest just pacified, someone like Fu should not yet leave; he was again made Frontier Commissioner concurrently Prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors argued that with Shu only just pacified, someone like Fu should not yet leave; he was again made Frontier Commissioner concurrently prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 再被召，逾年財抵建康，復引咎不進。

translations.literal: Summoned again, after more than a year he finally reached Jiankang, again citing fault and not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again, he took more than a year to reach Jiankang and once more pleaded fault and refused to proceed.

sentences.zh: 上召輔益堅，乃之鎮江俟命。

translations.literal: The emperor's summons to Fu grew ever firmer; he then went to Zhenjiang to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's summons grew ever more insistent, and Fu then went to Zhenjiang to await orders.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎楊簡言輔嘗棄成都，不當召，乃除兵部尚書兼侍讀，以龍圖閣學士知建康府兼江淮制置使。

translations.literal: Editing Assistant Yang Jian said that since Fu had once abandoned Chengdu, he should not be summoned; he was then appointed Minister of War concurrently Palace Reader, as Longtu Academician Prefect of Jiankang concurrently Yangzi-Huai Frontier Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Editing Assistant Yang Jian argued that since Fu had once abandoned Chengdu, he should not be recalled; Fu was then appointed Minister of War concurrently Palace Reader, Longtu Academician, prefect of Jiankang, and concurrently Yangzi-Huai Frontier Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，謚曰「莊惠」。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title "Solemn and Gracious."
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was granted the posthumous title "Solemn and Gracious."

sentences.zh: 劉光祖

translations.literal: Liu Guangzu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangzu

sentences.zh: 劉光祖，字德修，簡州陽安人。

translations.literal: Liu Guangzu, styled Dexiu, was a man of Yang'an in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangzu, whose style name was Dexiu, came from Yang'an in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼出於外祖賈暉，後以暉遺澤補官。

translations.literal: Raised young by his maternal grandfather Jia Hui, he later entered office through Hui's inherited grace.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from childhood by his maternal grandfather Jia Hui, he later entered office through the privilege Hui had bequeathed.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，廷對，言：「陛下睿察太精，宸斷太嚴，求治太速，喜功太甚。」

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; at the palace response he said: "Your Majesty's keen discernment is too fine, your imperial decisions too strict, your pursuit of good order too hasty, your delight in achievement too great.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he responded at the palace audience, saying, "Your Majesty's discernment is too sharp, your judgments too severe, your pursuit of good government too hurried, and your appetite for achievement too great.

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下躬擐甲胄，間馭毬馬，一旦有警，豈能親董六師以督戰乎？

translations.literal: He further said: "Your Majesty personally dons armor and occasionally rides polo horses—if alarm arises suddenly, can you personally direct the Six Armies to oversee battle?
translations.idiomatic: He further said, "Your Majesty personally dons armor and occasionally rides out for polo—if alarm should come suddenly, could you personally lead the Six Armies into battle?

sentences.zh: 夫人主自將，危道也。

translations.literal: For a sovereign to command in person is a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: For a ruler to take the field in person is a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 臣恐毬馬之事，敵人聞之，適以貽笑，不足以示武。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that in matters of polo, if enemies hear of it, it will only furnish them laughter—not enough to display martial prowess."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that if enemies hear of Your Majesty's polo riding, it will only make them laugh—it will not serve to display martial prowess."

sentences.zh: 除劍南東川節度推官，辟潼川提刑司檢法。

translations.literal: He was appointed legal officer of the Jiannan East Circuit military commission, then recruited as legal inspector of the Tongchuan judicial-intendancy office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed legal officer on the staff of the Jiannan East Circuit military commission and was later recruited as legal inspector for the Tongchuan judicial-intendancy office.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，召對，論恢復事，請以太祖用人為法，且曰：「人臣獻言，不可不察：其一，不量可否，勸陛下輕出驟進，則是即日誤國；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, summoned for audience, he discussed recovery affairs, requesting that Emperor Taizu's method of employing men be taken as model, and said: "When ministers offer counsel, it must not go unexamined: one kind—not measuring what is possible, urging Your Majesty to sally lightly and advance abruptly—this is to mislead the state that very day;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Chunxi reign, summoned for audience, he discussed the project of recovery and asked that Emperor Taizu's method of employing men be taken as the model, saying, "When ministers offer counsel, it must be examined carefully: one sort, failing to weigh what is possible, urges Your Majesty to sally lightly and advance rashly—this misleads the state at once;

sentences.zh: 其一，不思振立，茍且偷安，則是久遠誤國。」

translations.literal: another kind—not thinking to rouse and establish, seeking temporary ease and stealing peace—this is to mislead the state in the long run."
translations.idiomatic: another sort, unwilling to rouse the nation and build it up, settles for temporary ease and stolen peace—this misleads the state over the long term.

sentences.zh: 除太學正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Rectifier of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was appointed Rectifier of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 召試，守正字，兼吳、益王府教授，遷校書郎，除右正言、知果州。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination, he held the post of Standard-Bearer of Correct Characters, concurrently served as instructor to the Princes of Wu and Yi, was transferred to Collator, and was appointed Right Remonstrance Officer and Prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for a palace examination, he served as Standard-Bearer of Correct Characters and concurrently as instructor to the Princes of Wu and Yi, was transferred to Collator, and was appointed Right Remonstrance Officer and prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以趙汝愚薦，召入。

translations.literal: On Zhao Ruyu's recommendation, he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhao Ruyu's recommendation, he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，除軍器少監兼權侍左郎官，又兼禮部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Military Equipment, concurrently acting Left Attendant Gentleman in the Palace Secretariat, and also concurrently in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he was made Vice Director of the Directorate of Military Equipment, concurrently acting Left Attendant Gentleman in the Palace Secretariat, and also given concurrent duties in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時殿中侍御史闕，上方嚴其選，謂宰相留正曰：「卿監、郎官中有其人。」

translations.literal: At the time the post of Palace Attendant Censor was vacant; the emperor was strict in selecting for it and said to Chief Minister Liu Zheng: "Among your supervisors and gentleman-attendants there must be someone suited for it."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the post of Palace Attendant Censor was vacant, and the emperor, being strict in the selection, told Chief Minister Liu Zheng, "Among your supervisors and gentleman-attendants there must be someone fit for the post."

sentences.zh: 正沈思久之，曰：「得非劉光祖乎？」

translations.literal: Liu Zheng pondered a long while and said: "Could it not be Liu Guangzu?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng thought for a long while and said, "Could it not be Liu Guangzu?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「是久在朕心矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is indeed someone who has long been in my mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is indeed the man who has long been in my mind."

sentences.zh: 光祖入謝，因論：

translations.literal: Guangzu entered to give thanks and then discussed:
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu entered to give thanks and then addressed the throne:

sentences.zh: 「近世是非不明，則邪正互攻；

translations.literal: "In recent times, when right and wrong are unclear, the wicked and the upright attack one another;
translations.idiomatic: "In recent times, when right and wrong are unclear, the wicked and the upright turn on one another;

sentences.zh: 公論不立，則私情交起。

translations.literal: when public opinion is not established, private feelings rise up together.
translations.idiomatic: when public judgment has no standing, private attachments take hold.

sentences.zh: 此固道之消長，時之否泰，而實為國家之禍福，社稷之存亡，甚可畏也。

translations.literal: This is indeed the waxing and waning of the Way and the adversity or prosperity of the times—but in truth it is the fortune or calamity of the state and the survival or destruction of the altars of soil and grain. It is deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ebb and flow of the Way and the turning of fortune in the age—but in truth it decides the weal or woe of the state and the life or death of the altars of soil and grain. It is profoundly to be feared.

sentences.zh: 本朝士大夫學術議論，最為近古，初非有強國之術，而國勢尊安，根本深厚。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, the scholarly learning and discussions of officials and gentry most closely approach antiquity. At first there was no technique for strengthening the state, yet the national stature was honored and secure and the foundations were deep and firm.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, the learning and public debate of officials and gentry came closer to antiquity than ever before. There was no secret art of making the state strong, yet its stature remained honored and secure and its foundations deep and firm.

sentences.zh: 咸平、景德之間，道臻皇極，治保太和，至於慶曆、嘉祐盛矣。

translations.literal: Between the Xianping and Jingde reigns, the Way reached the supreme standard and governance preserved great harmony; by the Qingli and Jiayou reigns, it had reached its height.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xianping and Jingde reigns the Way reached its summit and governance preserved great harmony; by the Qingli and Jiayou eras it stood at its zenith.

sentences.zh: 不幸而壞於熙、豐之邪說，疏棄正士，招來小人，幸而元祐君子起而救之，末流大分，事故反覆。

translations.literal: Unfortunately it was ruined by the heterodox doctrines of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, which cast aside upright men and invited in petty men. Fortunately the gentlemen of the Yuanyou era rose to rescue it, but the later currents greatly divided and affairs repeatedly reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Then, alas, it was undermined by the perverse doctrines of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, which cast off upright men and welcomed petty ones. The gentlemen of the Yuanyou era rose to set things right, but the later currents split wide apart and affairs swung back and forth.

sentences.zh: 紹聖、元符之際，群凶得志，絕滅綱常，其論既勝，其勢既成，崇、觀而下，尚復何言。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng and Yuanfu eras, a host of villains had their way, extinguishing human relations and moral principle. Once their doctrines prevailed and their power was established, from the Chongning and Daguan reigns onward—what more need be said?
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaosheng and Yuanfu eras the villains had their day and human relations were all but extinguished. Once their doctrines prevailed and their power was secure, from the Chongning and Daguan reigns onward—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 臣始至時，聞有譏貶道學之說，而實未睹朋黨之分。

translations.literal: When your servant first arrived at court, I heard talk of ridiculing and denigrating the Learning of the Way, but in truth I had not yet seen factional division.
translations.idiomatic: When I first came to court, I heard talk of ridiculing and denigrating the Learning of the Way, but I had not yet seen the lines of faction drawn.

sentences.zh: 中更外艱，去國六載，已憂兩議之各甚，而恐一旦之交攻也。

translations.literal: In the midst of mourning for my mother abroad, I left the capital for six years. I already worried that the two factions had each grown extreme, and feared they might one day attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: Then, while mourning my mother away from court, I was absent from the capital for six years. I already feared that the two camps had each grown extreme and that one day they would turn on each other.

sentences.zh: 逮臣復來，其事果見。

translations.literal: When your servant returned, the matter indeed appeared as feared.
translations.idiomatic: When I returned, what I had feared came to pass.

sentences.zh: 因惡道學，乃生朋黨，因生朋黨，乃罪忠諫。

translations.literal: Because the Learning of the Way was hated, factions arose; because factions arose, loyal remonstrance was treated as crime.
translations.idiomatic: Hatred of the Learning of the Way bred factions; factions bred the criminalization of loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，以忠諫為罪，其去紹聖幾何！

translations.literal: Alas! To treat loyal remonstrance as crime—how far is this from the Shaosheng era!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—to treat loyal remonstrance as a crime, how far have we come from the Shaosheng era!

sentences.zh: 陛下履位之初，端拱而治，凡所進退，率用人言，初無好惡之私，豈以黨偏為主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's reign, you sat upright and governed. In all appointments and dismissals you generally followed the people's voice. At first there was no private favor or dislike—how could factional bias have been the guiding principle?
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Your Majesty's reign you governed with upright bearing. Appointments and dismissals generally followed public counsel, and at first there was no private favor or dislike—surely factional bias was not the guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 而一歲之內，逐者紛紛，中間好人固亦不少，反以人臣之私意，微累天日之清明。

translations.literal: Yet within a single year dismissals have come one after another. Among those removed, good men were certainly not few—and this has subtly blemished the clarity of Heaven's sun through the private feelings of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a single year dismissals have followed one after another. Many good men were among those removed, and the private feelings of ministers have subtly clouded the brightness of the imperial sun.

sentences.zh: 往往推忠之言，謂為沽名之舉；

translations.literal: Again and again, words offered in loyalty are called acts of seeking a reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Again and again, words offered in loyalty are dismissed as bids for reputation;

sentences.zh: 至於潔身以退，亦曰憤懟而然。

translations.literal: and even withdrawing to preserve one's integrity is said to be done out of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: and even withdrawing to preserve one's integrity is called the act of an embittered man.

sentences.zh: 欲激怒於至尊，必加之以訐訕。

translations.literal: To provoke the sovereign's anger, [opponents] are sure to add charges of impertinent criticism.
translations.idiomatic: To rouse the sovereign's wrath, they are sure to add charges of impertinent criticism.

sentences.zh: 事勢至此，循默乃宜，循默成風，國家安賴？

translations.literal: When affairs reach this point, keeping silent and going along becomes the appropriate course—but if keeping silent becomes the custom, on what can the state rely?
translations.idiomatic: When affairs reach this point, silence and compliance seem the safe course—but if silence becomes the custom, what will the state have to rely on?

sentences.zh: 臣欲熄將來之禍，故不憚反復以陳。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to extinguish the calamities to come, and therefore does not fear to state this repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to extinguish the calamities to come, and therefore do not shrink from saying this again and again.

sentences.zh: 伏幾聖心豁然，永為皇極之主，使是非由此而定，邪正由此而別，公論由此而明，私情由此而熄，道學之譏由此而消，朋黨之跡由此而泯，和平之福由此而集，國家之事由此而理，則生靈之幸，社稷之福也。

translations.literal: I humbly hope that the sacred heart may be opened wide and forever be the sovereign who embodies the supreme standard, so that right and wrong may be settled thereby, the wicked and upright distinguished thereby, public opinion clarified thereby, private feelings extinguished thereby, ridicule of the Learning of the Way dispelled thereby, traces of faction erased thereby, the blessings of peace gathered thereby, and the affairs of the state ordered thereby—then the good fortune of the people and the altars of soil and grain will follow.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty's sacred heart may open wide and that you may forever stand as the sovereign at the supreme standard, so that right and wrong are settled, wicked and upright are separated, public judgment is made clear, private attachments are stilled, ridicule of the Learning of the Way fades, the marks of faction disappear, the blessings of peace gather, and the affairs of state are put in order—then the people and the altars of soil and grain will know good fortune.

sentences.zh: 不然，相激相勝，展轉反復，為禍無窮，臣實未知稅駕之所。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, mutual provocation and mutual victory, turning back and forth without end—the calamity will be boundless, and your servant truly does not know where he may lay down his carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, provocation and counter-provocation will turn without end, and the harm will know no limit. I truly do not know where I may safely rest."

sentences.zh: 章既下，讀之有流涕者。

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, some who read it wept.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, some who read it were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 劾罷戶部尚書葉翥、太府卿兼中書舍人沈揆結近習，圖進用，言：「比年以來，士大夫不慕廉靖而慕奔競，不尊名節而尊爵位，不樂公正而樂軟美，不敬君子而敬庸人，既安習以成風，謂茍得為至計。

translations.literal: He impeached and had removed Minister of Revenue Ye Chu and Grand Steward concurrently Drafting Secretary Shen Kui for befriending close attendants and scheming for advancement, saying: "In recent years officials and gentry have not admired integrity and quiet rectitude but admired frantic competition; not honored reputation and integrity but honored rank and position; not delighted in public justice but delighted in soft flattery; not respected gentlemen but respected mediocre men. Having settled into this habit until it became custom, they take whatever they can get as the highest plan.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and had removed Minister of Revenue Ye Chu and Grand Steward Shen Kui, who also served as Drafting Secretary, for cultivating close attendants and scheming for advancement, saying, "In recent years officials and gentry have ceased to admire integrity and quiet rectitude and instead admire frantic competition; they no longer honor reputation and principle but honor rank and office; they no longer delight in public justice but delight in soft flattery; they no longer respect gentlemen but respect mediocrities. This habit has hardened into custom, and grasping whatever one can is taken as the highest wisdom.

sentences.zh: 良由前輩老成，零落殆盡，後生晚進，議論無所據依，學術無所宗主，正論益衰，士風不競。

translations.literal: This is truly because the elder generation of seasoned worthies has nearly all passed away, while the young and latecomers have no authority to rely on in debate and no master to follow in learning—orthodox discourse grows ever weaker and the spirit of the scholar class ever less competitive.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause is that the elder generation of seasoned worthies has nearly all passed away, while the young and the latecomers have no authority to lean on in debate and no master to follow in learning. Orthodox discourse grows weaker by the day, and the spirit of the scholar class no longer holds its own.

sentences.zh: 幸詔大臣，妙求人物，必朝野所共屬、賢愚所同敬者一二十人，參錯立朝，國勢自壯。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty may instruct the great ministers to seek out outstanding men with fine discernment—ten or twenty whom court and country alike look to and whom wise and simple alike equally respect—and place them at court in varied posts; then the nation's stature will strengthen of itself.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will command the chief ministers to seek out outstanding men with fine judgment—ten or twenty whom court and country alike look to and whom wise and simple alike revere—and place them at court in varied posts. Then the nation's strength will rise of itself.

sentences.zh: 臣雖終歲無所奏糾，固亦未至曠官。

translations.literal: Though your servant may go the whole year without submitting impeachments, I have still not reached the point of neglecting my office.
translations.idiomatic: Though I may go a whole year without submitting impeachments, I have still not neglected my duties.

sentences.zh: 今日之患，在於不封殖人才，臺諫但有摧殘，廟堂初無長養。

translations.literal: Today's affliction lies in not cultivating talent. The censorate and remonstrance offices only destroy, while the hall of government at first does nothing to nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Today's affliction is that talent is not cultivated. The censorate and remonstrance offices only tear down, while the hall of government does nothing to nurture.

sentences.zh: 臣處當言之地，豈以排擊為能哉？」

translations.literal: Your servant occupies a post where one must speak—how could taking destructive attacks as one's talent be right?"
translations.idiomatic: I hold a post where one is obliged to speak—how could destructive attack be my purpose?

sentences.zh: 徙太府少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 求去不已，除直秘閣、潼川運判。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested to leave and was appointed Compiler of the Direct Office of the Imperial Archives and Transport Judge of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to leave office and was appointed Compiler of the Direct Office of the Imperial Archives and transport judge of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 改江西提刑，又改夔州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Jiangxi Judicial Commissioner, then again changed to Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Jiangxi Judicial Commissioner, then again reassigned to Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗不豫，上久不過宮，光祖致書留正、趙汝愚曰：「宜與群賢並心一力，若上未過宮，宰執不可歸安私第。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong was ill and the emperor long failed to visit the palace, Guangzu wrote to Liu Zheng and Zhao Ruyu, saying: "You should join your hearts and strength with all worthy men. If the emperor has not yet visited the palace, the chief ministers must not retire in peace to their private residences.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong fell ill and the emperor long failed to visit the palace, Guangzu wrote to Liu Zheng and Zhao Ruyu, saying, "You should join hearts and strength with all worthy men. If the emperor has not yet visited the palace, the chief ministers must not retire in comfort to their private homes.

sentences.zh: 林、陳二閹，自以獲罪重華，日夜交諜其間。

translations.literal: The two eunuchs Lin and Chen, thinking themselves guilty before Chonghua Palace, day and night intrigue between the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The two eunuchs Lin and Chen, believing themselves guilty before Chonghua Palace, intrigue day and night between the two courts.

sentences.zh: 宜用韓魏公逐任守忠故事，以釋兩宮疑謗。

translations.literal: You should apply the precedent of Duke Han of Wei expelling Ren Shouzhong to dispel suspicion and slander between the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: You should follow the precedent of Duke Han of Wei expelling Ren Shouzhong to dispel suspicion and slander between the two palaces.

sentences.zh: 大臣亦當收兵柄，密布腹心，俾緩急有可仗者。」

translations.literal: The great ministers should also gather military authority, place trusted men throughout, so that in crisis there will be those to rely upon."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers should also gather military authority and place trusted men throughout, so that in an emergency there will be men to rely on."

sentences.zh: 聞孝宗崩，又貽書汝愚，勉以安國家、定社稷之事。

translations.literal: When word came that Xiaozong had died, he again wrote to Ruyu, urging him to matters of securing the state and stabilizing the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Xiaozong had died, he wrote again to Ruyu, urging him to secure the state and stabilize the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，除侍御史，改司農少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Attendant Censor and then changed to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong took the throne, he was appointed Attendant Censor and then made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 入對，獻《謹始》五箴。

translations.literal: Entering for audience, he presented the Five Admonitions on *Beginning with Care*.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he presented the Five Admonitions entitled *Beginning with Care*.

sentences.zh: 又論：「人主有六易：天命易恃，天位易樂，無事易安，意欲易奢，政令易怠，歲時易玩。

translations.literal: He further argued: "A ruler has six things easy [to fall into]: it is easy to rely on Heaven's mandate, easy to take pleasure in Heaven's throne, easy to feel secure when nothing is amiss, easy for desire to grow lavish, easy for government orders to grow slack, easy for seasonal observances to become trivial pastimes.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued, "A ruler faces six temptations: it is easy to rely on Heaven's mandate, easy to take pleasure in the throne, easy to feel secure when all is calm, easy for desire to turn extravagant, easy for government orders to slacken, and easy for seasonal rites to become mere amusements.

sentences.zh: 又有六難：君子難進，小人難退，苦言難入，巧佞難遠，是非難明，取舍難決。

translations.literal: There are also six difficulties: it is hard for gentlemen to advance, hard for petty men to withdraw, hard for bitter words to enter, hard for clever flatterers to be kept far, hard for right and wrong to be clarified, hard for choices to be decided.
translations.idiomatic: There are also six difficulties: gentlemen are hard to advance, petty men are hard to remove, bitter counsel is hard to accept, clever flatterers are hard to keep at a distance, right and wrong are hard to clarify, and choices are hard to decide.

sentences.zh: 暗主之所易，明主之所難；

translations.literal: What a dim ruler finds easy is what a bright ruler finds hard;
translations.idiomatic: What a dim ruler finds easy is precisely what a bright ruler finds hard;

sentences.zh: 暗主之所難，明主之所易。」

translations.literal: what a dim ruler finds hard is what a bright ruler finds easy."
translations.idiomatic: what a dim ruler finds hard is precisely what a bright ruler finds easy."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下以隆慈之命，踐祚於素幄，蓋有甚不得已者，宜躬自貶損，盡禮於上皇，使聖意歡然知釋位之樂，然後足以昭陛下之大孝。」

translations.literal: He further said: "Your Majesty, by the command of Longci, ascended the throne in the white mourning canopy—there was much that could not be helped. You should personally humble yourself and observe every rite toward the Retired Emperor, so that his sacred mind may delight in knowing the joy of yielding the throne—only then will Your Majesty's great filial piety be fully displayed."
translations.idiomatic: He further said, "Your Majesty ascended the throne in the white mourning canopy by Longci's command—much of it could not be helped. You should personally humble yourself and observe every rite toward the Retired Emperor, so that his sacred heart may delight in the joy of yielding the throne. Only then will Your Majesty's great filial piety shine forth.

sentences.zh: 上悚然嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor, startled, praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, startled, praised the counsel and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 進起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Diarist of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace diarist.

sentences.zh: 論：「政令當出中書，陛下審而行之，人主操柄，無要於此。」

translations.literal: He argued: "Government orders should issue from the Secretariat; Your Majesty should examine them and carry them out—the sovereign's grasp of authority has nothing more essential than this."
translations.idiomatic: He argued, "Government orders should come from the Secretariat; Your Majesty should examine them and put them into effect. There is nothing more essential to the sovereign's grasp of power than this.

sentences.zh: 知閤門事韓侂胄浸擅威福，故首及之。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou, Commissioner of the Gate, was gradually monopolizing power and favor—so he first named him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou, Commissioner of the Gate, was gradually monopolizing power and favor, and so Guangzu named him first.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Record-Keeper of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of Record-Keeper of the Left.

sentences.zh: 集議卜孝宗山陵，與朱熹皆謂會稽山陵，土薄水淺，乞議改卜。

translations.literal: At a collective deliberation on selecting Xiaozong's imperial tomb, he and Zhu Xi both held that the Kuaiji tombs had thin soil and shallow water, and asked that reselection be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: At a collective deliberation on selecting Xiaozong's imperial tomb, he and Zhu Xi both argued that the Kuaiji site had thin soil and shallow water and asked that a new site be considered.

sentences.zh: 既而熹與祠，光祖言：「漢武帝之於汲黯，唐太宗之於魏徵，仁宗之於唐介，皆暫怒旋悔。

translations.literal: When Xi was given a temple appointment, Guangzu said: "Emperor Wu of Han toward Ji An, Emperor Taizong of Tang toward Wei Zheng, and Emperor Renzong toward Tang Jie—all briefly grew angry and then quickly repented.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was given a temple appointment, Guangzu said, "Emperor Wu of Han with Ji An, Emperor Taizong of Tang with Wei Zheng, and Emperor Renzong with Tang Jie—all briefly grew angry and then quickly repented.

sentences.zh: 熹明先聖之道，為今宿儒，又非三臣比。

translations.literal: Xi illuminates the Way of the earlier sages and is the eminent Confucian of today—he is not to be compared with those three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xi expounds the Way of the earlier sages and is the leading Confucian of our day. He is not to be compared with those three ministers.

sentences.zh: 陛下初膺大寶，招徠耆儒，比初政之最善者。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first received the great treasure of the throne, you summoned venerable Confucians—this was among the best things of your early reign.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first received the throne, you summoned venerable Confucians—one of the finest acts of your early reign.

sentences.zh: 今一旦無故去之，可乎？」

translations.literal: Now to remove him without cause in a single day—can that be right?"
translations.idiomatic: To remove him without cause in a single day—can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 且曰：「臣非助熹，助陛下者也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant is not aiding Xi—I am aiding Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I am not defending Xi—I am defending Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 再疏，不聽。

translations.literal: He submitted again; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 劉德秀劾光祖，出為湖南運判，不就，主管玉局觀。

translations.literal: Liu Dexiu impeached Guangzu; he was sent out as Transport Judge of Hunan but did not accept and instead served as Superintendent of the Jade Bureau Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dexiu impeached Guangzu. He was sent out as transport judge of Hunan but declined the post and instead served as superintendent of the Jade Bureau Abbey.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚既罷相，侂胄擅朝，遂目士大夫為偽學逆黨，禁錮之。

translations.literal: After Zhao Ruyu was dismissed as chief minister, Tuozhou monopolized the court and thus labeled officials and gentry as the faction of false learning and treason, imprisoning them by prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Ruyu was removed as chief minister, Tuozhou dominated the court and labeled officials and gentry the faction of false learning and treason, banning and imprisoning them.

sentences.zh: 光祖撰《涪州學記》，謂：「學之大者，明聖人之道以修其身，而世方以道為偽；

translations.literal: Guangzu wrote the *Record of the Fuzhou Academy*, saying: "The great aim of learning is to illuminate the sages' Way to cultivate oneself—yet the age just now treats the Way as false;
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu wrote the *Record of the Fuzhou Academy*, saying, "The great purpose of learning is to illuminate the sages' Way and cultivate oneself—yet the age treats the Way as false;

sentences.zh: 小者治文章以達其志，而時方以文為病。

translations.literal: the lesser aim is to craft writing to express one's purpose—yet the times just now treat literature as a disease.
translations.idiomatic: the lesser purpose is to craft writing to express one's intent—yet the times treat literature as a sickness.

sentences.zh: 好惡出於一時，是非定於萬世。」

translations.literal: Likes and dislikes come from a single moment; right and wrong are fixed for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Likes and dislikes arise in a moment; right and wrong are settled for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 諫官張釜指為謗訕，比之楊惲，奪職，謫居房州。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Zhang Fu cited this as slander, comparing him to Yang Yun; his office was stripped and he was banished to live in Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Zhang Fu denounced this as slander and compared him to Yang Yun. Guangzu was stripped of office and banished to Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，許自便。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was permitted to return at will.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was permitted to return at will.

sentences.zh: 起知眉州，復職，將漕利路，以不習邊事辭。

translations.literal: He was raised to serve as Prefect of Meizhou, restored to office, and was about to become Transport Commissioner of Lizhou Circuit but declined on grounds of unfamiliarity with frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Meizhou, restored to office, and was about to become transport commissioner of Lizhou Circuit but declined on grounds of unfamiliarity with frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 進直寶謨閣，主管沖佑觀。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the Direct Office of the Hall of Precious Illumination and served as Superintendent of the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to the Direct Office of the Hall of Precious Illumination and made superintendent of the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，光祖白郡守，焚其榜通衢，且馳告帥守、監司之所素知者，仗大義，連衡以抗賊。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, Guangzu informed the prefect, burned his proclamations in the public thoroughfare, and swiftly notified military commissioners, prefects, and circuit supervisors he had long known, upholding the great principle and joining in alliance to resist the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, Guangzu informed the prefect, burned his proclamations in the public thoroughfare, and swiftly notified the military commissioners, prefects, and circuit supervisors he had long known, upholding the great principle and joining in alliance to resist the rebel.

sentences.zh: 俄聞曦誅，則以書屬宣撫使楊輔，講行營田，前日利歸吳氏者，悉收之公上，以省餉軍費；

translations.literal: Soon word came that Xi had been executed; he then wrote to Military Commissioner Yang Fu urging implementation of garrison farming—all profits that had formerly gone to the Wu clan were to be recovered for the public exchequer to save military rations and expenses;
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Xi had been executed. He then wrote to Military Commissioner Yang Fu urging the establishment of garrison farming and the recovery for the public exchequer of all profits that had formerly gone to the Wu clan, so as to save military rations and expenses;

sentences.zh: 獎名節、旌死事以激忠烈之心。

translations.literal: reward integrity of character and honor those who died in service to stir the hearts of the loyal and heroic.
translations.idiomatic: he also urged that integrity be rewarded and those who died in service be honored, so as to stir the hearts of the loyal and heroic.

sentences.zh: 除潼川路提刑、權知瀘州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Judicial Commissioner of Tongchuan Circuit and acting Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial commissioner of Tongchuan Circuit and acting prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，召除右文殿修撰、知襄陽府，進寶謨閣待制、知遂寧府，改京湖制置使，以寶謨閣直學士知潼川府。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, he was summoned and appointed Compiler of the Right Culture Hall and Prefect of Xiangyang, advanced to Gentleman at the Hall of Precious Illumination and Prefect of Suining, changed to Frontier Commissioner of Jinghu, and as Direct Academician of the Hall of Precious Illumination made Prefect of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed, he was summoned and appointed compiler of the Right Culture Hall and prefect of Xiangyang, advanced to Gentleman at the Hall of Precious Illumination and prefect of Suining, made Frontier Commissioner of Jinghu, and finally, as Direct Academician of the Hall of Precious Illumination, prefect of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 詔以閔雨求言，光祖奏：「女真乃吾不共戴天之仇，天亡此仇，送死於汴。

translations.literal: An edict sought advice on drought; Guangzu memorialized: "The Jurchens are the enemy with whom we cannot share Heaven—Heaven is destroying this enemy, sending it to its death at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict sought counsel on drought, Guangzu memorialized, "The Jurchens are the enemy with whom we cannot share Heaven. Heaven is destroying this enemy and sending it to its death at Bian.

sentences.zh: 陛下為天之子，不知所以圖之，天與不取，是謂棄天，未有棄天而天不我怒也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Heaven's son, yet does not know how to plan against them. Heaven gives and you do not take—this is called abandoning Heaven, and there has never been one who abandoned Heaven without Heaven's anger upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Heaven's son, yet does not know how to seize the opportunity. Heaven offers and you refuse—this is to abandon Heaven, and no one has ever abandoned Heaven without Heaven's wrath falling upon him.

sentences.zh: 青、鄆、藺、會求通弗納，陛下為中國衣冠之主，人歸而我絕之，是謂棄人，未有棄人而人不我怨也。

translations.literal: Qing, Yun, Lan, and Hui sought contact and were not received. Your Majesty is lord of Chinese robes and caps—people come and you reject them. This is called abandoning the people, and there has never been one who abandoned the people without their resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, Yun, Lan, and Hui sought contact and were turned away. Your Majesty is lord of the civilized realm—people come and you reject them. This is to abandon the people, and no one has ever abandoned the people without earning their resentment.

sentences.zh: 且金人舍其巢穴，汙我汴京，尚可使吾使人拜之於祖宗昔日朝會之廷乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Jin people abandoned their nests and defiled our Bian capital—can we still send our envoys to bow to them in the hall where our ancestors once held court?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jin abandoned their own nests and defiled our capital at Bian—can we still send our envoys to bow to them in the hall where our ancestors once held court?"

sentences.zh: 又請改正憲聖慈烈皇后諱日。

translations.literal: He also asked that the taboo day of Empress Xiansheng Cilie be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the mourning day of Empress Xiansheng Cilie be corrected.

sentences.zh: 先是，后崩以慶元三年十一月二日，郊禋期迫，或謂侂胄曰：「上親郊，不可不成禮。

translations.literal: Previously the empress died on the second day of the eleventh month of the third year of Qingyuan; the suburban sacrifice drew near, and someone said to Tuozhou: "The emperor's personal suburban sacrifice cannot fail to be completed as ritual requires.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the empress had died on the second day of the eleventh month of the third year of Qingyuan. With the suburban sacrifice imminent, someone said to Tuozhou, "The emperor's personal suburban sacrifice cannot fail to be completed.

sentences.zh: 且有司所費既夥，奈何已之？」

translations.literal: And the expense of the relevant offices is already great—how can it be stopped now?"
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices have already spent so much—how can the rite now be halted?"

sentences.zh: 侂胄入其言，五日祀圜丘，六日始宣遺誥。

translations.literal: Tuozhou accepted this advice. On the fifth day he sacrificed at the Circular Altar; only on the sixth day was the dying edict promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou accepted this advice. On the fifth day the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Altar; only on the sixth was the dying edict promulgated.

sentences.zh: 於是光祖言：「憲聖，陛下之曾祖母，克相高宗，再造大業。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangzu said: "Xiansheng was Your Majesty's great-grandmother. She aided Emperor Gaozong and restored the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Guangzu said, "Xiansheng was Your Majesty's great-grandmother. She aided Emperor Gaozong and restored the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 侂胄敢視之如卑喪，遷就若此。

translations.literal: Yet Tuozhou dared treat her as a low-ranking mourning case and shift the observance thus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tuozhou dared treat her mourning as a lesser case and shift the observance in this way.

sentences.zh: 賊臣就戮，盍告謝祖宗，改從本日？」

translations.literal: The traitor has now been executed—why not report and give thanks to the ancestors and revert to the actual date?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that the traitor has been executed, why not report to the ancestors and give thanks, and revert to the true date?

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 升顯謨閣直學士、提舉玉隆萬壽宮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Illumination and made Superintendent of the Yulong Longevity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Illumination and made superintendent of the Yulong Longevity Palace.

sentences.zh: 引年不許，提舉西京嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: His request to retire on grounds of age was not granted; he was made Superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His request to retire on grounds of age was denied, and he was made superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十五年卒，進華文閣學士，謚「文節」。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiading he died, was posthumously advanced to Academician of the Hall of Flowering Culture, and given the posthumous title "Cultured and Restrained."
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Jiading, was posthumously advanced to Academician of the Hall of Flowering Culture, and granted the posthumous title "Cultured and Restrained."

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚稱光祖論諫激烈似蘇軾，懇惻似范祖禹，世以為名言。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu said that Guangzu's remonstrance and counsel were as fierce as Su Shi's and as earnest and compassionate as Fan Zuyu's—the age has taken this as a fine saying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu said that Guangzu's remonstrance was as fierce as Su Shi's and as earnest and compassionate as Fan Zuyu's—a remark the age has taken as a fine saying.

sentences.zh: 所著《後溪集》十卷。

translations.literal: His writings included the *Houxi Collection* in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the *Houxi Collection* in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子：端之、靖之、翊之、竑之。

translations.literal: Sons: Duanzhi, Jingzhi, Yizhi, and Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Duanzhi, Jingzhi, Yizhi, and Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：徐誼竄逐於小人之手，身之否，道之亨也。

translations.literal: The historian comments: Xu Yi was banished by the hands of petty men—personally it was denial, for the Way it was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Xu Yi was driven out by petty men—personally it was misfortune, for the Way it was triumph.

sentences.zh: 吳獵之以學為政，項安世之通經博古，皆一時之英才，今更定舊史，公論其少伸歟！

translations.literal: Wu Lie's taking learning as government, Xiang Anshi's mastery of the classics and broad knowledge of antiquity—both were outstanding talents of their time. Now that the old histories are being revised, has public opinion at last been somewhat vindicated!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lie governed through learning; Xiang Anshi mastered the classics and ranged broadly over antiquity—both were outstanding talents of their age. Now that the old histories are being revised, has public judgment at last been somewhat vindicated!

sentences.zh: 薛叔似通儒也，不幸以開邊事累之。

translations.literal: Xue Shusi was a thorough Confucian, unfortunately burdened by the frontier-opening affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shusi was a thorough Confucian, unfortunately tarnished by the frontier-opening affair.

sentences.zh: 劉甲、楊輔蔚乎有用之才。

translations.literal: Liu Jia and Yang Fu were abundantly men of practical talent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jia and Yang Fu were men of abundant practical talent.

sentences.zh: 劉光祖盛名與《涪州學記》並傳穹壤，世之人何憚而不為君子也！

translations.literal: Liu Guangzu's great fame and the *Record of the Fuzhou Academy* are transmitted together throughout heaven and earth—what would people of the age fear that keeps them from becoming gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangzu's great fame and the *Record of the Fuzhou Academy* will be handed down together through heaven and earth—what would people of this age fear that keeps them from choosing the way of the gentleman!
